title: Catalog API pagination contract decision
purpose: Document the two competing catalog API pagination drafts for GET /v1/items and the unresolved choice of authoritative contract, so the pagination contract can be selected and implemented against.

scope.text: Catalog API draft A: GET /v1/items returns a JSON object with an items array and next_cursor string. UI must support moving to the next page.
Catalog API draft B: GET /v1/items returns a top-level JSON array and uses page and page_size query parameters.

requirements.text: Catalog API draft A: GET /v1/items returns a JSON object with an items array and next_cursor string.
UI must support moving to the next page.
Catalog API draft B: GET /v1/items returns a top-level JSON array and uses page and page_size query parameters.

stories.text: If a human selects draft A as the authoritative contract, a UI developer can fetch items and advance through pages using a cursor-based response.
acceptance_criteria: Given a human has selected draft A as the authoritative contract, when GET /v1/items is called, then the response body is a JSON object containing an items array and a next_cursor string.
Given a human has selected draft A as the authoritative contract, when the response's next_cursor indicates further results, then the UI can move to the next page and retrieve the subsequent items.

stories.text: If a human selects draft B as the authoritative contract, an API consumer can fetch items and navigate pages using page and page_size query parameters.
acceptance_criteria: Given a human has selected draft B as the authoritative contract, when GET /v1/items is called, then the response body is a top-level JSON array.
Given a human has selected draft B as the authoritative contract, when GET /v1/items is called with page and page_size query parameters, then the response reflects that page selection.

dependencies.text: Neither draft is approved; the authoritative contract has not been selected.

risks.text: Selecting draft A satisfies the object-with-items-and-next_cursor response shape but leaves the page and page_size parameter expectation from draft B unmet; selecting draft B satisfies the array response and page parameters but leaves the items array and next_cursor expectation from draft A unmet.

open_questions: Which draft should a human select as the authoritative contract for GET /v1/items: draft A (items array plus next_cursor) or draft B (top-level array with page and page_size parameters)?
Who has authority to select the authoritative contract?
